name: Carrion Defense Works Autonomous Mine Clearance System
product_name: Carrion Defense Works Autonomous Mine Clearance System
description: An autonomous ground vehicle that detects, identifies, and neutralizes mines and improvised explosive devices without human presence. The AMCS uses ground-penetrating radar, chemical sniffing sensors, and magnetic anomaly detection to locate buried ordnance, then deploys robotic manipulators or focused explosive charges to neutralize the threat. The vehicle is heavily armored against blast damage and can continue operating after triggering detonations that would kill a human operator. Carrion developed it for post-conflict zone clearance but it is equally effective for clearing improvised explosive threats in urban environments.
social_impact: The AMCS has made mine clearance safer but has also lowered the barrier to mine deployment — knowing that clearance is automated rather than requiring human risk reduces the political cost of mining an area. The technology has also revealed the extent of improvised explosive threats in lower-tier districts, where the AMCS has detected ordnance densities that suggest systematic mining of residential areas by unknown parties.
story_hooks: An AMCS clearing a Tier 1 route has discovered a mine field that was not improvised — the mines are military-grade Vespid SIM-2 units, and their placement pattern suggests professional military deployment in a civilian area.
An AMCS has been hacked and reprogrammed to deploy mines rather than clear them — the clearance vehicle is now mining the routes it was supposed to make safe.
